blanks.sentence: Ultra-processed food is described as food containing _____.
These foods have been connected with _____.
One sign is that the food may contain five or more _____.
Ingredient labels may include substances such as _____, preservatives, additives, dyes and sweeteners.
A major reason for the popularity of ultra-processed food is _____.
A _____ can be put in the microwave and heated very quickly.
By contrast, cooking a _____ from the beginning may take much longer.
Chocolate, biscuits or cake may be called a _____ when someone enjoys them but feels they should not.
The suggested approach is not panic, but eating everything in _____.

multipleChoice.question: How is ultra-processed food initially characterised?
options: It contains artificial ingredients such as additives or sweeteners.
It is always cooked in restaurants before being sold.
It contains only natural ingredients prepared at home.
It is mainly food that has lost its original flavour.

multipleChoice.question: What health concern is raised about ultra-processed foods?
options: They make people dislike fresh food immediately.
They are dangerous only when eaten at breakfast.
They have been associated with poor health and diseases such as obesity and diabetes.
They mainly cause problems because they are difficult to digest.

multipleChoice.question: Which feature helps identify an ultra-processed food according to the reporter?
options: It is served cold and needs no preparation.
It is made with exactly three ingredients.
It is sold only in large supermarkets.
It includes several ingredients not normally found in an average kitchen.

multipleChoice.question: Why do the speakers say they now try to cook more themselves?
options: They want to copy restaurant-style ready meals.
They want more control over what goes into their food.
They believe snacks are always more expensive than meals.
They think chocolate should be eaten only during programmes.

multipleChoice.question: Why are ready meals used to explain the popularity of ultra-processed food?
options: They show how quickly convenient food can be prepared.
They prove processed food is usually healthier than fresh food.
They show that microwave meals require advanced cooking skills.
They explain why people no longer enjoy hot food.

multipleChoice.question: What does Annabel’s “guilty pleasure” example show?
options: She believes sweet foods should be banned completely.
She eats chocolate only because it is cheap and convenient.
She enjoys some processed treats despite feeling she probably should not.
She thinks biscuits and cake are healthier than ready meals.

multipleChoice.question: How are ready meals contrasted with cooking from scratch?
options: Ready meals require more preparation but taste fresher.
Cooking from scratch is described as faster but less reliable.
Both methods are said to take the same amount of time.
Ready meals are quicker, while cooking from scratch takes longer.

multipleChoice.question: Why is ultra-processed food described as a tricky topic?
options: Experts cannot identify which foods are processed.
It involves a trade-off between health concerns and practical appeal.
People agree that processed food tastes bad but is healthy.
It is difficult because processed food is rare in daily life.

multipleChoice.question: What is the purpose of Hannah’s question about crisps?
options: To ask whether occasional enjoyment is acceptable or complete avoidance is needed.
To prove that crisps are the healthiest ultra-processed snack.
To argue that people should eat crisps every day.
To compare crisps with fizzy drinks historically.

multipleChoice.question: What final advice is given about eating ultra-processed foods?
options: Avoid every processed product immediately.
Eat processed snacks whenever they are cheap.
Stay calm and avoid having too much of anything.
Replace all home-cooked meals with ready meals.
